steamRestartNote: Steam is never force-killed and shortcuts.vdf is never written while Steam runs. The same installation is reopened after shutdown, including when the shortcut operation fails.

setupWizardDescription: Run the guided Linux setup again.
wizardWelcomeBody: This unofficial Linux port guides you through the pieces the installer needs. It uses Monkellie's tf2vr-linux backend and never bundles game files.
wizardWelcomeFeature1: Detects Titanfall 2 and the Linux backend
wizardWelcomeFeature2: Checks Proton, OpenXR, WiVRn and Steam
wizardWelcomeFeature3: Skips anything already configured and can be reopened later
wizardGameBody: Titanfall 2 must be installed through Steam so Proton can run it. The detector looks in your Steam libraries and the backend's saved game path.
wizardGameMissingDetail: Install Titanfall 2 in Steam, launch it once normally, then check again. If it lives in a non-Steam prefix, the backend can still be configured manually.
wizardBackendBody: The app manages a verified checkout of Monkellie's tf2vr-linux project. Verification checks its origin and required files; it does not install the mod yet.
wizardDependenciesNotRunDetail: Run the read-only backend check to confirm Proton and the required runtime pieces. You can review its output here.
wizardDependenciesRetryHint: Review the output above, fix what the backend reports, then run the check again. You can also skip this step and return later.
wizardOpenXrMissingDetail: Install and configure SteamVR, WiVRn or Monado, then check again. VR cannot launch without an OpenXR runtime.
wizardWiVrnBody: WiVRn lists VR games through a desktop entry. The entry must include the X-WiVRn-VR category; this app adds or repairs it without touching the game.
wizardWiVrnNotDetectedDetail: Install WiVRn, then return here to add its desktop entry. You can also use SteamVR or Monado instead.
wizardWiVrnAfterInstall: Install the mod first; the WiVRn entry is created after the tf2vr launcher exists.
wizardSteamNeedsLauncherDetail: The shortcut points at ~/.local/bin/tf2vr, which the backend creates after a successful install. You can add it later from Settings.
wizardReleaseBody: Stable follows the latest release. Beta follows the latest beta build. You can change this at any time on the installer screen.
wizardReleaseChooseDetail: Choose Stable or Beta, then continue. The selection is saved as the exact backend token.
wizardReleaseUnavailableDetail: Verify the backend or refresh the catalogue in the installer, then choose a release there.
wizardFinishTitle: You're ready for the next step
wizardFinishBody: Review the setup summary. Missing optional integrations are fine; missing game, backend, OpenXR or dependency checks will block VR installation.
wizardReadyBody: The core pieces are in place. Continue to the installer to choose a release and install.
wizardNotReadyBody: You can finish setup later from Settings. The installer will show the same missing pieces before it installs.

notificationWiVrnIssueBody: The WiVRn desktop entry is missing or incomplete. Use Repair WiVRn entry in Settings.
notificationInstallFailedBody: Installing {0} failed (exit code {1}). Open installation history for details.
helpChannelsBody: Stable follows tested releases. Beta follows newer preview builds and may contain bugs. Switching keeps the release you selected.
helpPinnedBody: A pinned release stays on one exact version. Use it when a newer release causes problems; it does not update automatically.
helpProtonBody: Proton-TF2VR is a separate Proton prefix created by the tf2vr-linux helper. It holds the mod's Windows environment and is used by the launcher; it is not the normal Titanfall 2 prefix.
helpProtonRebuildBody: A rebuild recreates the separate Proton-TF2VR prefix when it is missing or broken. It resets prefix-local settings, but does not delete Titanfall 2 or campaign saves.
helpWiVrnBody: WiVRn must be running before you launch so it can provide the OpenXR session and list the entry. The desktop entry only registers Titanfall 2 VR for WiVRn.
helpSteamRestartBody: Steam keeps shortcuts in memory and rewrites its shortcut file on exit. The installer closes Steam gracefully, updates the shortcut, then reopens the same installation. Other games and shortcuts are preserved.
